limits: a plugin is read at session start: a session that was already open when it was installed or rewritten loads it after `/reload-plugins`, not before

`installed` means enabled at USER scope; a project's own .claude/settings.json can set `enabledPlugins["openwalkietalkie@openwalkietalkie"]: false` and turn it off for that repository, which this row cannot see

this row reads Claude Code's own records (installed_plugins.json, known_marketplaces.json, enabledPlugins) and never runs the CLI; `claude plugin list --json` is the authority on what a session actually loads

trust and enablement come from codex's own `hooks/list` (trustStatus, enabled, warnings) whenever codex can be run, because deckd cannot compute a hook's hash itself (C14a) and only codex tells `trusted` from `modified` or sees the warnings that mean the whole hooks.json was discarded (C12, C18)
the absence of a SessionStart is NOT evidence that hooks are dead: SessionStart fires on a session's first turn, not when it opens (C18), so an idle session legitimately produces none

trust is positional (<event>:<group>:<handler>) and keyed on the REALPATH of hooks.json; any change to deckd's path, timeout, matcher or statusMessage re-breaks it as `modified` and the hooks stop firing with no notice (C14a)
